newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on SMR20 sales.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on SMR20 sales.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher on Thursday, bolstered mainly by sales of SMR20 to European and Asian clients, trade sources said.
Activity was limited in the afternoon, but prices remained firm on sales reported in early trading, the sources said.
A government trade source said a June shipment of 1,500 tonnes of SMR20 was reported sold to Britain at 262 Malaysian/Singapore cents ($1.05) per kg.
Another two shipments of 2,500 tonnes each of SMR20 was sold to Turkey and Beijing at 267 cents per kg, said the source.

At the close, June RSS 1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 277.50 cents a kg, unchanged from Tuesday's close. June SMR 20 buyer closed at 264, up 1.50 cents from Tuesday.
The Malaysian market was closed on Wednesday for a holiday.
Traders quoted the SMR20 at 261, SMR CV at 330, SMR 5 at 272, SMR L at 307, SMR 10 at 262 and drum latex at 227.
The INRO five-day moving indicator was quoted at 213.96 on May 21, against 213.51 on May 20. The daily indicator fell to 212.79 from 213.66. -- K. Baranee (603-230-7509) ($1 = 2.50 ringgit)
